papers.title_en: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching: Gradient Flows and Geodesics in Wasserstein Space
papers.evidence: 通过Wasserstein几何统一扩散与流匹配的理论
papers.tldr: 生成模型中的扩散与流匹配均植根于Wasserstein空间的几何结构。该空间赋予概率测度Riemannian流形，其测地线即为最优传输路径。扩散模型通过自由能梯度流（即Fokker-Planck方程）的JKO离散化实现，统一了DDPM、DDIM等算法。流匹配则直接学习测地线，沿直线进行确定性ODE采样，大幅减少步数。该几何视角将两类模型纳入同一框架：扩散是初值问题，流匹配是边值问题，但到达相同目标分布。
papers.abstract_en: The space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d$) of probability measures with finite second moment carries a natural geometry: the quadratic Wasserstein distance W_2 makes it a complete metric space and, following Otto, a (formal) Riemannian manifold whose geodesics are the optimal-transport interpolations. On this manifold, the gradient flow of the free energy F(rho) = KL(rho || π) is exactly the Fokker-Planck equation, and its implicit-Euler discretization is the JKO scheme. This is the geometry underlying diffusion models: the forward process descends the free energy, and each denoising step realizes one JKO step, which recovers DDPM, DDIM, NCSN/SMLD, and Energy Matching; this is one scheme, not separate theories. The same manifold supports a second variational principle. Its geodesics - the minimum-action curves of the Benamou-Brenier formula - are precisely the optimal-transport paths that Flow Matching learns. Fixing both endpoints and following the geodesic, generation becomes a deterministic ODE along a straight line, hence far fewer sampling steps. Placing both families of models on one manifold makes their relationship exact: diffusion follows a free-energy gradient flow, an initial-value problem; optimal-transport Flow Matching follows a Wasserstein geodesic, a boundary-value problem. The two reach the same endpoints along different paths.

papers.title_en: Introduction to Stochastic Differential Equations for Generative Machine Learning: A Variational Perspective
papers.authors: Ole Winther, Paul Jeha, Sander Dieleman, Andriy Mnih, Manfred Opper, Andrea Dittadi
papers.evidence: 从变分视角涵盖扩散模型、评分匹配和流匹配，为流体动力学中的生成模型提供基础方法。
papers.tldr: 生成式机器学习中，常微分与随机微分方程推动图像、视频等生成任务。本文从变分视角自包含地介绍微分方程、概率框架及Fokker-Planck方程，推导ELBO作为统一框架。扩散模型、得分匹配、流匹配均可视为该变分框架的特定参数化。通过一维密度建模实例比较不同参数化，提供直观理解与实用指导。
papers.abstract_en: The use of ordinary and stochastic differential equations has led to substantial progress in generative machine learning with applications to, for example, image, video and biomolecule generation. This paper provides a self-contained and informal introduction to the differential equations, the probabilistic framework for using them in generative modeling and the Fokker--Planck equation that governs the temporal evolution of the marginal distribution of the stochastic variables of the differential equations. The variational lower bound on the log-likelihood (the evidence lower bound, ELBO) is derived and used as a general starting point for a discussion of diffusion models, score matching, and flow matching. All of these approaches may be viewed as specific parameterizations of the most general variational approach. A one-dimensional density modeling problem is used as a simple example to compare different parameterizations.
